newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bomb blast near Islamist centre in Lebanon camp.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast near Islamist centre in Lebanon camp.

text.p: A small bomb exploded overnight near a centre for Lebanese Moslem fundamentalists in the southern port city of Sidon causing little damage but no casualties, security sources said on Tuesday.
They said the blast occurred near the main office of the pro-Syrian al-Ahbash Sunni group inside the country's largest Palestinian refugee camp of Ail el-Hilweh.

It was not immediately known who was behind the incident, which came three days after Lebanon's highest court sentenced to death the Palestinian head of a rival Sunni group and three of his supporters -- two Lebanese and a Palestinian -- for the 1995 murder of al-Ahbash leader Nizar al-Halabi.

The Judicial Council convicted Palestinian Ahmed Saadi, resident of Ein el-Hilweh and head of Esbat al-Ansar group, of ordering the killing of Sheikh Halabi who was shot dead in his car in Beirut on August 1995.
Esbat al-Ansar (Band of Supporters) blasted the court order and said suspects were forced to make their confessions under torture.

"We, at the Islamic Esbat al-Ansar reject the court rulings against our brothers as they were based on confessions obtained under psychological and physical torture," the group said in a statement sent by fascimile to an international news agency in Beirut, the group said:

The Judicial Council, whose rulings cannot be appealed, had opened the trial of 20 group members -- of whom Saadi and two others are at large -- in May 1996 on charges of killing Halabi and belonging to a violent armed group.
